newsitem.title: USA: APL Q4 fully diluted shr runs a profit.
newsitem.headline: APL Q4 fully diluted shr runs a profit.

text.p: NOTE: (1) During the fourth quarter of 1996, the company recorded gains of $11.5 million and $9.2 million from the sale of certain cranes from its terminals in Los Angeles and Oakland, and residential property in Singapore, respectively.
In addition, during 1996, the company recorded gains of $12.9 million in the third quarter and a net loss of $0.3

million in the fourth quarter resulting from the curtailment of pension and post-retirement obligations due to workforce reductions, a second quarter gain of $6.9 million on the sale of its domestic distribution services segment, and a first quarter gain of $1.6 million on a vessel sale.

During the fourth quarter of 1995, the company recorded a restructuring charge of $48.4 million related to the acceleration of its program to reengineer its order cycle processes and other organizational changes.
The company incurred costs related to its corporate initiatives, not included in the restructuring charge, of $6.6
million and $24.9 million the fourth quarter and year of 1995, respectively.

During the 1995 fourth quarter and full year, the company recognized gains of $2.5 million and $6.2 million on vessel sales, respectively, and received liquidated damages resulting from the delayed delivery of two of the new C11-class vessels of $2.0 million and $5.5 million, respectively.
(2) The provision for income taxes has been calculated using the effective tax rate estimated for the respective years.

The company's estimated income tax rates for 1996 and 1995 were 33 percent and 43 percent, respectively. The 1996 effective tax rate was reduced during the third and fourth quarters primarily to reflect additional tax credits, which became available, and deductions.
During the fourth quarter of 1995, the company's effective tax rate of 43 percent reflects the increased effect of nondeductible items on lower income.
(3) During the third and fourth quarters of 1996, the company repurchased a total of 1.3 million shares of its common stock.
In July 1995, 1.5 million outstanding shares of the company's 9 percent Series C Cumulative Convertible Preferred Stock ("Series C Stock") were converted into 4 million shares of common stock.
Primary Earnings Per Share for the full year of 1995 include the deduction of $3.4 million for the Series C Stock dividends.
Fully Diluted Earnings Per Share for 1995 reflect the conversion of the Series C stock as though it had occurred as of the beginning of the year.
Additionally, in August through October 1995, the company repurchased a total of 6 million shares of its common stock.
